questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of conducting a “time audit” as described in the chapter?

options.text: To compare your time habits with those of your friends
To understand how you are currently spending your 24 hours each day
To immediately change all unproductive habits
To create a strict daily schedule without flexibilityCorrect Answer:B) To understand how you are currently spending your 24 hours each day

questions.question_text: Which activity is recommended in the chapter to get a detailed view of how you spend a single day?

options.text: Weekly Overview
24-Hour Time Log
24-Hour Time Log

questions.question_text: According to the chapter, which of the following is a common time-waster for high school students?

options.text: Attending classes regularly
Excessive screen time on social media or videos
Completing homework on time
Participating in extracurricular activitiesCorrect Answer:B) Excessive screen time on social media or videos

questions.question_text: What is one way the chapter suggests to minimize a time-waster like social media?

options.text: Avoid using social media completely for a month
Set a specific time limit, such as 20 minutes per day, using a timer
Use social media only during peak productivity hours
Replace social media with more screen time on educational appsCorrect Answer:B) Set a specific time limit, such as 20 minutes per day, using a timer

questions.question_text: What does recognizing productivity patterns help you do, according to the chapter?

options.text: Spend more time on leisure activities without guilt
Schedule important tasks during your peak energy times
Avoid working in environments with any distractions
Focus only on tasks during the morning hoursCorrect Answer:B) Schedule important tasks during your peak energy times

questions.question_text: Why does the chapter emphasize starting with small changes after assessing time habits?

options.text: Small changes are less noticeable to others
Big changes are impossible to achieve for high school students
Small changes are more manageable and can build into lasting habits
Small changes require no effort or planningCorrect Answer:C) Small changes are more manageable and can build into lasting habits
